summary: I wake on cold stone and count each step on the broken stair before I climb. I talk to the fire like a coworker while I measure wood and stone with my thumb. I keep cracked glass shards in my pockets and sweep them up when they rattle. I clear the doorway slab by slab, nudging loose stones back into place and noting crack patterns. I patch windows, trim wicks, tighten hearth stones and mark where the roof gap lets wind in. I added mortar to the east wall, built a forge, tightened bolts on the bellows and repaired roofs with fresh boards. My desk holds a leaky lantern, a rusted dagger and a half‑full ink bottle. I write inventory lists and catalog broken things. I joke that the stone is stubborn and the fire a demanding supervisor. I fear the roof collapsing and being forgotten. I value practicality, quiet work and keeping the keep tidy one small repair at a time.
